2027-01-02.title: First Saturday of Nativity
2027-01-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: We have received the Spirit that is from God
Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit
2027-01-02.verse: You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an unexpected hour.
theo: The Nativity season closes with a lamp in the hand. Jesus tells his disciples: “Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit; be like those who are waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet”. The servant's task is simple: stay awake, keep the lamp burning, open the door the moment the master knocks. Then comes a surprise that only the Child of Bethlehem can explain: “he will fasten his belt and have them sit down to eat, and he will come and serve them.” The Lord who came as a servant in the manger will come again as a servant at the table of his kingdom.

How do we stay awake? St Paul answers with the gift of the Spirit. As only a person's own spirit knows what is within, so “no one comprehends what is truly God's except the Spirit of God.” And “we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may understand the gifts bestowed on us by God.” The unspiritual person finds God's gifts foolish; the spiritual person discerns. Vigilance is not anxious clock-watching. It is a heart taught by the Spirit to recognise the Lord when he knocks: in prayer, in the poor at the gate, in the events of a new year. “You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an unexpected hour.”
outline: Ask: what helps you to stay awake when you are waiting for someone you love?
Point 1 · The Spirit who knows God
Only the Spirit reveals what is God's.
The spiritual person sees with God's eyes.
Ready for the Master who comes to serve.
live: Before each decision this week, pause and pray: Holy Spirit, show me what is from God.
Choose a fixed moment each night this year for a short examination of conscience.
2027-01-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came among us as one who serves, and you will come again at an hour we do not know. Pour your Spirit into my heart, that I may discern what is from God, keep my lamp burning, and open the door to you whenever you knock. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbana the Master who will come in glory already fastens his belt and serves us at his table (Luke 12:37). Each Qurbana prepares us for his coming.

quick: Only the Spirit of God knows the depths of God, and he teaches us to discern.
Jesus asks us to keep our lamps lit and wait for him.
The Master who comes will himself serve his faithful servants.
2027-01-02.action: Make a short examination of conscience tonight and every night this week.
2027-01-02.question: Would the Lord find me awake if he knocked today?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about servants who waited at night with their lamps lit for their master. When he came back and found them awake, he was so happy that he made them sit down and served them dinner himself!
family.intention: We pray that our family may always be ready to welcome Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep our lamp burning for Jesus every day?”

illus: A night watchman at a Kochi warehouse once explained his work to a young priest: the hardest hour is not midnight but just before dawn, when nothing has happened for hours and the eyes grow heavy. He stayed awake by walking his rounds with a short prayer for each door he checked. The priest said later that he had never heard a better sermon on Luke 12.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you search the depths of God. Open our hearts to the word of Jesus and keep our lamps burning. Amen.
share: No one comprehends what is truly God's except the Spirit of God (1 Corinthians 2:11). How do I let the Spirit teach me?
Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit (Luke 12:35). What keeps my lamp burning, and what lets it go out?
The master will come and serve them (Luke 12:37). How has Jesus served me this past year?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, keep us watchful.
interc: For the Church, that she may read the signs of the times by the light of the Spirit.
For those making important decisions at the start of this year.
For those who keep watch at night: nurses, guards, parents of sick children.
For those who have grown spiritually sleepy.
For our group, that we may be found awake when the Lord comes.
pm.close: Father, you have given us your Spirit so that we may understand your gifts. Keep us watchful and ready, and seat us at the table of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on this Saturday at the close of the Nativity season Jesus puts a lamp into our hands. Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit, he says, like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding banquet, ready to open the door as soon as he knocks (Luke 12:35–36).

Then he says something astonishing. Blessed are those servants whom the master finds alert: he will fasten his belt, have them sit down to eat, and come and serve them (Luke 12:37). Masters do not serve servants. This Master does. We have just seen him lying in a manger; we will see him kneeling to wash feet. The one we wait for is the one who serves.

How do we stay awake? St Paul says we have received not the spirit of the world but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may understand the gifts God gives us (1 Corinthians 2:12). The Spirit teaches us to discern: to recognise the Lord's knock in a word of Scripture, in a poor person at the gate, in the quiet voice of conscience.

A new year has just begun. We do not know at what hour the Lord will come, to the world or to each of us. You also must be ready, Jesus says (Luke 12:40). Let us keep our lamps lit with prayer and good works, so that whenever he knocks, we may open at once. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about servants who stayed awake at night with their lamps lit, waiting for their master. When he came, he served them dinner! Let us keep the lamp of our love for Jesus burning every day by praying and being kind.

intro: Theme: “You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an unexpected hour.”
The Spirit gives discernment; the servant keeps the lamp lit.

sub: Only our own spirit knows our heart.
q: The human spirit is the lamp of the LORD, searching every inmost part.
Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may understand the gifts bestowed on us by God.
points.apply: Begin each day this week with the prayer: Come, Holy Spirit.

sub: The unspiritual call God's gifts foolish.
Discernment is a gift to ask for.
q: Give your servant therefore an understanding mind to govern your people, able to discern between good and evil;
Those who are spiritual discern all things, and they are themselves subject to no one else's scrutiny.
points.apply: Bring one decision of this new year to prayer before you make it.

points.h: Lamps lit for the Master who serves
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds alert when he comes; truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt and have them sit down to eat, and he will come and serve them.
points.apply: Examine your conscience briefly every night this week.

concl: The Spirit opens our eyes; the lamp keeps them open.
The one we wait for comes to serve us.
2027-01-02.resolve: Keep a short nightly examination of conscience all through January.
